title: Compatible truncated coefficient sections over a perfect residue field
statement: Let $p$ be prime and let $f:R\to S$ be a local homomorphism of nonzero commutative local rings of characteristic $p$, meaning $f^{-1}(\mathfrak m_S)=\mathfrak m_R$, with $\mathfrak m_R^u=0$ and $\mathfrak m_S^v=0$ for some positive integers $u,v$. A local ring here has one maximal ideal. Put $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$ and $l=S/\mathfrak m_S$, and let $\bar f:k\hookrightarrow l$ be the induced residue-field map. Assume $k$ is perfect, meaning every element of $k$ is a $p$th power. There are ring homomorphisms $s_R:k\to R$ and $s_S:l\to S$ such that their composites with the residue maps are the identities and $f\circ s_R=s_S\circ\bar f$. Fields and field extensions use [def-pc-field-extension].

source.place: Tag 09EZ, lemma-cohen, compatible section assertion, specialized to perfect lower residue field (so the upper residue extension is separable in the general field-extension sense).

proof.text: Both residue fields have characteristic $p$. The prime field $\mathbf F_p$ is perfect: Frobenius fixes every element, since it is a ring map fixing $1$. For each finitely generated intermediate field of $k/\mathbf F_p$ and of $l/k$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-perfect-field-separating-basis] to the perfect lower field. Each such intermediate extension is separably generated. Thus both $k/\mathbf F_p$ and $l/k$ are separable in exactly the possibly transcendental sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension].

source.place: Tag 09EZ, lemma-cohen, proof: separable residue fields are formally smooth; nilpotent lifting expanded through powers of the maximal ideal.

proof.text: Give $R$ and its quotients their prime-field algebra structures. Construct $\mathbf F_p$-algebra maps $a_n:k\to R/\mathfrak m_R^n$ reducing to the identity in $k$, for $1\le n\le u$. Set $a_1=\mathrm{id}_k$. Given $a_n$ with $n<u$, put $D=R/\mathfrak m_R^{n+1}$ and $J=\mathfrak m_R^n/\mathfrak m_R^{n+1}$. The quotient $D/J$ identifies with $R/\mathfrak m_R^n$: send the class of the class of $r$ to its class modulo $\mathfrak m_R^n$; this is well-defined and bijective since its kernel is precisely $J$. Moreover $J^2=0$ since $2n\ge n+1$. Apply [lem-sfb-separable-field-square-zero-lifting] to $k/\mathbf F_p$, $D,J,a_n$ to obtain $a_{n+1}$ reducing to $a_n$. At $n=u$, $\mathfrak m_R^u=0$ identifies the target with $R$ and gives $s_R$. Its reduction is $a_1$, so it is a residue section.

source.place: Tag 09EZ, lemma-cohen, proof: separable residue fields are formally smooth; nilpotent lifting expanded through powers of the maximal ideal.

proof.text: Make $S$ a $k$-algebra by $f\circ s_R$. The quotient $l=S/\mathfrak m_S$ then has structure map $\bar f$, because for $a\in k$ its image is $\operatorname{res}_S(f(s_R(a)))=\bar f(\operatorname{res}_R(s_R(a)))=\bar f(a)$. Thus the identity $l\to S/\mathfrak m_S=l$ is a $k$-algebra map. These are the quotient algebra structures of [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient].

source.place: Tag 09EZ, lemma-cohen, proof: separable residue fields are formally smooth; nilpotent lifting expanded through powers of the maximal ideal.

proof.text: Construct $k$-algebra maps $b_n:l\to S/\mathfrak m_S^n$ for $1\le n\le v$, starting with $b_1=\mathrm{id}_l$. For $n<v$ use $D=S/\mathfrak m_S^{n+1}$ and $J=\mathfrak m_S^n/\mathfrak m_S^{n+1}$; the representative calculation of step 2 identifies $D/J$ with $S/\mathfrak m_S^n$, and $J^2=0$ again follows from $2n\ge n+1$. Apply [lem-sfb-separable-field-square-zero-lifting] now to the separable extension $l/k$ and $b_n$, obtaining $b_{n+1}$ as a $k$-algebra map. At $n=v$ obtain $s_S:l\to S$ because $\mathfrak m_S^v=0$. Reduction gives $b_1=\mathrm{id}_l$. Finally, the defining algebra-map equation gives $s_S(\bar f(a))=f(s_R(a))$ for every $a\in k$, proving the required compatibility.
